message.content: A cell that contains more than one nucleus is called a **multinucleated cell**. In many contexts this is referred to as a **syncytium** (literally “joined together”), especially when the nuclei arise from the fusion of several cells. A common example in pathology is the multinucleated giant cell, which forms during chronic inflammation.
